newsitem.title: USA: American Air in pact to buy Shuttle.
newsitem.headline: American Air in pact to buy Shuttle.

text.p: American Airlines said Thursday it agreed to buy Shuttle Inc., the commuter airline linking New York, Washington and Boston operated by U.S. Airways Group Inc.
American, a unit of AMR Corp., said it will purchase the stock, warrants and debt of Shuttle Inc. for an undisclosed price.
Shuttle Inc., formerly the Trump Shuttle, was taken over in April 1992 by a group of lenders. US Airways operates the shuttle under a management contract and holds 47 percent of the equity.
American said the deal is contingent upon US Airways' decision not to exercise its option to purchase the Shuttle or its right to match American's offer.
In April, US Airways started to assess the value of the Shuttle, which operates in one of the nation's busiest travel corridors, but made no decision whether to buy the commuter service.
US Airways' exclusive right to buy the Shuttle ended April 9, but the airline has the right to match any purchase offer by another party following the deadline.
US Airways could not be immediately reached for comment.
Although the Shuttle is a small property, it offers American a foothold in the East Coast's frequent flyer business market, said Candace Browning, an airline analyst with Merrill Lynch.
"It's a clever move for American," she said.
However, she added, the deal could fall apart.
"It's a very complicated process and may take a very long time to sort out. It's not at all certain that American will emerge as the victor."
In early trading, AMR Corp.'s stock was unchanged at $96.875 a share and U.S. Airways was up 12.5 cents at $34.75 a share, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
